ucs.title: [LLM] Turla PowerStallion OneDrive WebDAV C2 — net.exe mounting *.live.net as backup channel
ucs.description: Hunts Turla's PowerStallion lightweight PowerShell backdoor, which mounts an attacker OneDrive folder over WebDAV via `net use https://*.live.net` and uses it as a fallback C2 / dead-drop to manage their flagship implants (Carbon, ComRAT). Mounting a Microsoft OneDrive WebDAV endpoint as a drive from an interactive user context is a Turla-characteristic living-off-trusted-cloud move.
ucs.splunk:
| tstats `security_content_summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.process_name=net.exe OR Processes.process_name=net1.exe) Processes.process="*use*" (Processes.process="*docs.live.net*" OR Processes.process="*onedrive.live.com*" OR Processes.process="*d.docs.live.net*" OR Processes.process="*.live.net*") by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.parent_process_name Processes.process_name Processes.process Processes.process_hash
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| where NOT match(user,"\$$")
| convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
| sort - lastTime
ucs.kql:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where FileName in~ ("net.exe","net1.exe")
| where ProcessCommandLine has "use"
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("docs.live.net","onedrive.live.com","d.docs.live.net",".live.net")
| where AccountName !endswith "$"            // exclude machine accounts — PowerStallion runs as the interactive user
| where AccountName !in~ ("system","local service","network service")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine,
          ParentImage = InitiatingProcessFolderPath,
          ParentCmd   = InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
ucs.sentinel_kql:
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where NewProcessName endswith "\\net.exe" or NewProcessName endswith "\\net1.exe"
| where CommandLine has "use"
| where CommandLine has_any ("docs.live.net","onedrive.live.com","d.docs.live.net",".live.net")
| where SubjectUserName !endswith "$"
| where SubjectUserName !in~ ("system","local service","network service")
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, SubjectUserName, NewProcessName, CommandLine, ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc
ucs.sigma_yaml:
title: Turla PowerStallion OneDrive WebDAV Mount via net.exe
id: 6b3f2c1a-9d44-4a7e-bf21-7c0e1a2b3d4f
status: experimental
description: Detects net.exe/net1.exe mounting a Microsoft OneDrive WebDAV endpoint as a drive, consistent with Turla PowerStallion fallback C2.
references:
  - https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G0010/
author: SOC Detection Engineering
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection_img:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\net.exe'
      - '\net1.exe'
  selection_cmd:
    CommandLine|contains: 'use'
  selection_dest:
    CommandLine|contains:
      - 'docs.live.net'
      - 'onedrive.live.com'
      - 'd.docs.live.net'
      - '.live.net'
  condition: all of selection_*
falsepositives:
  - Users legitimately mounting personal OneDrive via WebDAV
level: high
tags:
  - attack.command_and_control
  - attack.t1102
  - attack.t1071.001
  - attack.g0010
ucs.datadog_query: source:windows.sysmon @EventID:1 @Image:(*\\net.exe OR *\\net1.exe OR *\\NET.EXE) @CommandLine:(*use* AND (*docs.live.net* OR *onedrive.live.com* OR *d.docs.live.net* OR *.live.net*))
ucs.falcon_logscale_query:
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 ImageFileName=/\\net1?\.exe$/i
| regex("(?i)\\buse\\b", field=CommandLine)
| regex("(?i)(docs\\.live\\.net|onedrive\\.live\\.com|d\\.docs\\.live\\.net|\\.live\\.net)", field=CommandLine)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, CommandLine], function=count())
ucs.rationale: PowerStallion's WebDAV-mounted OneDrive C2 is a documented, Turla-specific tradecraft (ESET reporting) — generic APTs use HTTP/S beacons or cloud SDKs, not an interactive `net use` against *.live.net to a WebDAV share. The net.exe + live.net + interactive-user combination is extremely rare in benign enterprise traffic, giving a low-FP, alert-grade signature tightly bound to G0010.

ucs.title: [LLM] Turla ComRAT v4 Gmail-web-UI C2 — non-browser process beaconing to mail.google.com
ucs.description: Hunts Turla's ComRAT v4 (Agent.BTZ lineage) 'mail mode', which steals the victim's browser cookies and drives the Gmail web interface (mail.google.com) over HTTP to read base64/PDF-encoded commands and exfiltrate data. A non-browser binary repeatedly contacting Gmail web endpoints is a ComRAT-defining behaviour and a Turla hallmark of abusing legitimate webmail for stealthy C2.
ucs.splunk:
| tstats `security_content_summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Web.Web where (Web.url="*mail.google.com*" OR Web.dest="mail.google.com" OR Web.url="*googleusercontent.com*") NOT (Web.app IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","iexplore.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe","msedgewebview2.exe")) by Web.src Web.dest Web.url Web.app Web.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| where count > 1
| convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
| sort - lastTime
ucs.kql:
let Browsers = dynamic(["chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe","iexplore.exe","msedgewebview2.exe","chromium.exe"]);
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where RemoteUrl has_any ("mail.google.com","googleusercontent.com")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ (Browsers)
| where not(InitiatingProcessFolderPath has_any ("\\Program Files\\Google\\","\\Program Files (x86)\\Microsoft\\Edge\\","\\Mozilla Firefox\\"))
| summarize HitCount = count(), FirstSeen = min(Timestamp), LastSeen = max(Timestamp),
            Urls = make_set(RemoteUrl, 10), RemoteIPs = make_set(RemoteIP, 10)
          by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| where HitCount > 1     // automated polling of the Gmail web UI, not a one-off resolve
| order by HitCount desc
ucs.sentinel_kql:
let Browsers = dynamic(["chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe","iexplore.exe","msedgewebview2.exe"]);
ImWebSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where Url has_any ("mail.google.com","googleusercontent.com")
| where isnotempty(HttpRequestHeaderUserAgent)
| where not(HttpRequestHeaderUserAgent has_any ("Chrome/","Firefox/","Edg/","Safari/"))   // ComRAT uses a static/non-browser UA
| summarize HitCount = count(), FirstSeen = min(TimeGenerated), LastSeen = max(TimeGenerated),
            UAs = make_set(HttpRequestHeaderUserAgent, 10)
          by SrcIpAddr, SrcHostname, SrcUsername, DstHostname
| where HitCount > 1
| order by HitCount desc
ucs.datadog_query: source:windows.sysmon @EventID:3 @DestinationHostname:(*mail.google.com* OR *googleusercontent.com*) -@Image:(*\\chrome.exe OR *\\Chrome.exe OR *\\msedge.exe OR *\\firefox.exe OR *\\Firefox.exe OR *\\iexplore.exe OR *\\brave.exe OR *\\opera.exe OR *\\msedgewebview2.exe)
ucs.falcon_logscale_query:
#event_simpleName=DnsRequest DomainName=/(mail\.google\.com|googleusercontent\.com)$/i
| NOT (ContextImageFileName=/\\(chrome|msedge|firefox|brave|opera|iexplore|msedgewebview2|chromium)\.exe$/i)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ContextImageFileName], function=count())
| count > 1
ucs.rationale: ComRAT v4's defining innovation (ESET, 2020) is driving the Gmail web UI with stolen cookies as a bidirectional C2 channel — distinct from APT29/Cozy Bear OAuth abuse or APT41 cloud SDKs. Most legitimate Gmail traffic originates from real browser processes; a non-browser binary polling mail.google.com isolates the ComRAT cookie-replay behaviour to Turla/Secret Blizzard. Tagged hunting (not alertin
